title: runtime: add selector v2 telemetry (metrics + trace annotations) with sampling + label bucketing
author: Omar El-Sayed
description:
Summary: Adds first-class observability for kernel selector decisions (selector v1/v2) via (1) metrics with strict label bucketing, and (2) trace annotations/events for per-request debugging. This is required for staged rollout of kernel auto-selection v2 so we can correlate kernel choice with latency/correctness without blowing up cardinality.

Motivation/Context: Kernel selector v2 is table-driven and depends on model family + seq-length regime + GPU SKU. During canary we need to answer: (a) which kernel was chosen, (b) which inputs drove that decision, (c) what fallback path was taken (v2->safe set->v1), and (d) whether changes correlate with p95 regressions or correctness flags (NaNs). Prior instrumentation was log-only and not consistent across runtime components.

What this PR adds: 1) Metrics (Prometheus): - redwood_runtime_kernel_selector_decisions_total{selector_version,decision_outcome,model_family,seq_bucket,gpu_sku_norm,kernel_id_bucket} - redwood_runtime_kernel_selector_fallback_total{from_version,to_version,reason_bucket} - redwood_runtime_kernel_selector_registry_load_success{result,registry_version} - redwood_runtime_kernel_selector_registry_entries{registry_version} - redwood_runtime_kernel_selector_selection_latency_ms{selector_version,seq_bucket} (histogram)

2) Trace annotations (OpenTelemetry): - Adds span attributes on the existing "runtime.inference" span (and "runtime.prefill"/"runtime.decode" spans when present): selector.version, selector.model_family, selector.seq_bucket, selector.gpu_sku_norm, selector.kernel_id (sampled), selector.decision_outcome, selector.fallback_reason (when applicable). - Emits a lightweight event "kernel_selector.decision" with a structured payload for sampled requests only. - Adds a helper to attach selector decision context to traces without requiring callers to know about label bucketing logic.

3) Sampling + label bucketing: - Default metrics are always emitted, but high-cardinality dimensions are bucketed: kernel_id -> kernel_id_bucket (top-N allowlist + "other"); model name is NOT emitted. - Trace attributes that could be high-cardinality (kernel_id, raw gpu sku string, raw model id) are only attached under sampling OR are normalized/bucketed. - Sampling policy: selector decision trace details are recorded at 1% by default for hosted; 0% for dedicated unless explicitly enabled. This is configurable via runtime config (see below). - Adds a "debug" mode for internal canary where sampling can be temporarily increased (bounded at 10%) with an explicit config guard.

4) Config knobs: - runtime.selector.telemetry.enabled (default true) - runtime.selector.telemetry.trace_sampling_rate (default 0.01) - runtime.selector.telemetry.include_kernel_id_in_traces (default false; requires sampling) - runtime.selector.telemetry.kernel_id_allowlist (top N, defaults populated with current v1/v2 kernel ids)

5) Tests: - Unit tests for bucketing/normalization utilities (gpu sku normalization uses existing mapping from pr_18463; this PR consumes the normalized value only). - Snapshot-style tests to ensure metrics label sets remain stable (prevents accidental cardinality regression). - A small integration test that asserts span attributes are present when tracing is enabled and sampling selects the request.

Notes on cardinality controls (review request): This PR intentionally does not expose raw model_id/model_name in any metric label. model_family is from the taxonomy mapping and seq_bucket is a fixed enum. gpu_sku_norm is normalized to a small set (L4, A10, A100-40GB, A100-80GB, H100-SXM, H100-PCIe, OTHER). kernel_id_bucket is allowlisted to top-N + other to keep the label space bounded even as we add kernels.

Rollout/Operations: - No behavior change to selection logic. - Metrics land behind the existing runtime metrics pipeline. - Trace annotations respect the runtime tracing enablement flag and the new sampling knob. - Dashboards/alerts are not included here; those will land in ENG-3933 / INT-2331.

Follow-ups: - Once we have stable canary data, we should consider making the kernel_id allowlist auto-generated from the registry version (with an explicit cap) to reduce manual updates. - Consider adding a correctness counter that increments when we detect NaN/inf guards trip in the model output path, keyed by selector_version + seq_bucket (no kernel id).

Checklist: - [x] Metrics added and documented inline - [x] Trace annotations added (sampled) - [x] Cardinality review: labels bucketed, no model name leakage - [x] Unit tests + span integration test - [x] Backward compatible defaults
commits: runtime/telemetry: add selector telemetry metric definitions + label bucketing helpers
runtime/selector: plumb SelectorDecision into inference context for metrics/tracing
runtime/tracing: add kernel_selector.decision event + sampled attributes
runtime/config: add selector telemetry config options with validation + sane defaults
tests: snapshot tests for metric label sets; trace attribute integration test
conversation:
Grace Kim (review): Can we confirm we are not emitting model_id anywhere? We got burned by that in the scheduler tags last quarter. Omar El-Sayed (author): Confirmed. No model_id/model_name labels. model_family only (enum). I added a unit test that fails if someone tries to add model_id to metric label set.

Thomas Baird (review): kernel_id_bucket allowlist feels manual. What happens when we add new kernels during rollout? Omar El-Sayed (author): New kernel ids will fall into "other" until allowlist is updated. For canary we mostly care about selector_version + seq_bucket + gpu. Kernel id is mainly for debugging, so bucket=other is acceptable; also raw kernel id in traces is gated behind sampling + include_kernel_id_in_traces.

Logan Wright (review): Trace attributes: please avoid attaching kernel_id even when sampled unless a flag is on. Some customers mirror spans into their own backends and this could still be sensitive operational detail. Omar El-Sayed (author): Updated: kernel_id is now excluded by default even on sampled traces; requires runtime.selector.telemetry.include_kernel_id_in_traces=true.

Allison Grant (review): Metrics naming: prefer *_total for counters and use a consistent prefix. Also add decision_outcome and fallback_reason buckets as enums, not free-form strings. Omar El-Sayed (author): Done. Renamed counters and replaced string reasons with ReasonBucket enum; updated docs.

Aisha Bello (review): Can you add an example Grafana query snippet to the doc so SRE can build panels quickly? Omar El-Sayed (author): Added 3 example queries in runtime/docs/telemetry/kernel_selector.md (decision rate by selector_version; fallback rate; heatmap-like breakdown by gpu_sku_norm + seq_bucket).

Final approvals: Logan Wright (APPROVED), Allison Grant (APPROVED), Grace Kim (APPROVED)
release_notes: Internal-only: Adds metrics + sampled trace annotations to observe kernel selector decisions (selector v1/v2). No change to selection behavior; includes strict label bucketing and sampling controls to prevent cardinality blowups.
